name: Joe Leffert
kind: found and refused
fact: The 1989 Talisman photographs him. Printed p. 91 carries a Phonathon picture whose caption names two people: 'Big Red encourages Nashville, Tenn. senior Alyson Hyatt and Madison, Ind. junior Joe Leffert to bring in more money during the Phonathon. $96,215 was raised, topping the $60,000 goal.' Two figures are at the phones. The left one is plainly a woman and would be Hyatt on the usual left-to-right reading; the right one, in glasses, would be Leffert. It is not used, for two reasons: the caption carries no position word, so which figure is which rests on convention alone, and the right-hand face is a blurred three-quarter profile about 90 pixels across with a telephone handset across the jaw. A misidentified face is worse than no face. A later pass with a better scan of this page could revisit it.

name: Cinnamon Roberts

name: THE VOLUME-AT-A-TIME SWEEP OF 1988-1993, AND WHAT IT SETTLES
kind: method that worked, and a definitive negative
fact: Every leaf of six Talismans was rendered from the embedded scan and OCR'd with ocrmac at twice native size, and the whole worklist was then matched against the result in one pass instead of person by person: 1988 (389 leaves), 1989 (189), 1990 (375), 1991 (190), 1992 (185) and 1993 (144), 1,472 leaves and 127,157 lines of text. Cost about forty minutes of machine time with four sweeps running at once, roughly 1.2 seconds a page. IT WORKS AND IT SHOULD BE THE DEFAULT. It found in one pass what eight person-by-person passes had missed, and it produces a negative that can be trusted. THE THREE THINGS IT TURNED UP THAT THE INDEX ROUTE COULD NOT. First, the 1988 volume had never been swept by this block at all. It covers 1987-88, the year BEFORE the earliest cohort here, which is exactly where the 1988-89 intake sit as freshmen and sophomores, and it is where Elaine Burge's portrait was, in the freshman grid on p. 347. Always work the volume before the first year of service, not only the years of service and after. Second, the portrait grids are keyed to margin name blocks that the back index does not always index, so a person absent from an index can still be in a grid, and the reverse. Third, an organisation photograph with a positional caption is a portrait source, not just a name list, and the write-off entry in _archive-gaps.json about thirty-one members of 1990-91 to 1994-95 is wrong on that point: it reasons that a person 'named in an index but only on organization or story pages ... never sat for a portrait', which is true of the grids and does not mean there is no usable face. Ginger Markham was written off that way and her face is on 1993 p. 202. WHAT THE SWEEP PROVES NEGATIVELY: the following people are in NO portrait grid of any of the six volumes, checked line by line at the exact alphabetical position with fuzzy matching for OCR damage, and in most cases are absent from the volumes entirely. Amy McLoud, Brian Thornton, Chris Gaddis, Diane Robinson, Georgia Childress, Honor Logsdon, John Lindsey, Johnna Shirley, Lori Easton, Mark Spader, Mickie Hennig, Ron Hennig, Scott Hutchison, Chris Summerville, Jo Wood, Maribel Torres, Todd Gion, Allyson Adams, Andy Gowins, Angie Berry, Angie Sell, Aubrey Harris, Brent Weaver, Derrick Holt, Jeffrey Sanders, Julie Wedge, Mills Brockman, Nita Doshi, Richard Parish, Traceyealeen Garrett, Wallace Brown, Wendy Townsend, Wil Gramm, Brent Weeden, Chad Reagan, Chris Gibson, Chris Sweeney, Greg Butler, Gwendolyn Griffin, James Lindsey, Kristen Graves, Maryann D'Anielle, Melony Johnson, Melony Shemberger, Randy Elassal, Richard Parrish, Scott Ballard, Wilson Covington, Darron Brawner, Dawn Dillard, Derrek Duncan, Jason Sikes, Jeff Carlisle, Jeff Duncan, Jenny Stelmach, Jill Howard, Jill Reading, Jim Lee, Kendra Welch, Kim Mann, Laura Nunn, Margaret Carter, Molly Schreiner, Nicki Jerome, Paula Miller, Shawn Pinkston, Susanne Jeffiers, Thomas Lally, Tim Sturm, Trent Lyda, Von Parrish. For several the volumes hold a near neighbour that will tempt a later pass and is a different person: Sherry and Nicole Gaddis but no Chris; Dana, Rebekah, Clarence and Emily Shirley and a Shirley Green but no Johnna; Ann Michele Dillard but no Dawn; Anne, Lori Ann, James T. and Lisa Duncan and a Duncan Gibson but no Derrek and no Jeff; Amy, Kelley, Vikki, Jeffery, Willie, Reece, Donald, Charles, James, Melissa, Juliane and Tricia Carter but no Margaret; Sherry Woods, Karen Wood, Donna Wood and JoAnn Woodruff but no Jo Wood; Devon and Laura Pinkston but no Shawn; Loretta Welch but no Kendra; Jeff Schreiner but no Molly; Justin Carlisle but no Jeff; Stacey Brawner but no Darron; Sondra Jeffries but no Susanne. DO NOT RE-RUN THIS. If a later pass wants to re-check, the OCR is reproducible in forty minutes with scripts of about sixty lines; what is not worth doing again is looking these names up one at a time.

name: THE 1986 AND 1987 TALISMANS ON ARCHIVE.ORG ARE THE BEST SOURCE THIS BLOCK HAS
kind: source found, and it is four times the resolution of anything else here
fact: archive.org holds the Talisman for 1943-1981, 1986 and 1987 and NOTHING between 1988 and 1993, checked against its advanced-search API on 4 September 2026: talisman1988west through talisman1993west all return empty metadata. So the note in _archive-gaps.json that says to prefer archive.org copies over TopSCHOLAR for 1982-1991 cannot be followed for the volumes that cover this block's own years; those must come off TopSCHOLAR at about 96 dpi. But 1986 and 1987 CAN, and they scan at 3282 by 4500 pixels a page against TopSCHOLAR's 880, which is nearly four times the linear resolution. THAT CHANGES WHAT COUNTS AS A USABLE GROUP PHOTOGRAPH. A face in a fifteen-person club picture, worth 30 pixels on a TopSCHOLAR page and therefore worthless, comes out 200 pixels here. Three of this run's finds are from the 1987 volume and all three are far better than anything cut from 1988-1993: Becky Shirley's sophomore portrait at 360 by 435, Lisa Kaufman at 187 by 250 out of a thirteen-woman Alpha Delta Pi group, Joe Leffert at 205 by 295 out of a fifteen-person University Scholars group. Use scripts/talisman.py, which searches the OCR text stream and maps a hit back to a leaf; search the surname alone, and treat the leaf it returns as a pointer only, because the text stream pools captions from several leaves away. The reliable route is the back index: search 'Surname,' to get the index line, which gives printed page numbers, then pull leaf = page + 3. WHO THIS SEAM IS FOR: anyone whose first SGA year is 1988-89 or 1989-90 was at Western in 1986-87, and the whole 1988-89 cohort of this block was run against both volumes on this pass. Blocks whose people served 1985-86 to 1987-88 should work these two volumes before anything else.

name: Mickie Hennig
kind: written off with positive evidence: she sat for no portrait
fact: She is in the Talismans and she is not photographed, and the shape of the evidence makes that near certain rather than merely unfound. The 1987 index reads 'Hennig, Kathryn Michelle 316' and gives no second page; p. 316 is the Juniors divider, pulled and read at 3282 pixels on the archive.org copy, and it carries a full-page overhead photograph of a print sale in the Downing University Center, an essay on the junior year, and a pull quote signed '- Mickie Hennig' in the left margin. There is no portrait of her on it and no photograph of any named person. Being a junior in 1986-87 makes her a senior in 1987-88, so the 1988 volume is where her senior portrait would be; every one of its 389 leaves was OCR'd on this run and the only Hennig anywhere in the book is her brother or namesake Ron, in the University Scholars caption on p. 159. She is absent from the 1989, 1990, 1991, 1992 and 1993 volumes entirely. Secretary of ASG in 1988-89 and there is no picture of her.

kind: source checked and closed for identification
fact: Board three of stu_org/322 is the one that looks like the answer and is not. It has the Kappa Delta 'Congratulations 1994-95 Spirit Masters' newspaper advertisement pasted in the centre, with the whole class named in two columns, and about thirty cut-out photographs pasted around it. name: THE SPIRIT MASTERS CLASS COMPOSITES ARE ONE NAME TO ONE FACE, AND NOBODY HAD FOUND THEM
kind: source found, the strongest identification available anywhere in this era
fact: TopSCHOLAR stu_org/321 is the WKU Spirit Masters scrapbook for 1989-90 (UA12/2/16, article 1322, 154 MB through the Wayback route, seventy boards). Its fourth board is the class COMPOSITE: twenty-four studio portraits pasted in five ranks, and beside each portrait is a printed strip giving the person's name, home town, class and major. One name against one face, no counting, no row-and-column reasoning, no sex test - the strongest identification this archive accepts, and it is on a board scanned at 4209 by 3474, so a single portrait crops out at about 370 by 400 with no upscaling. The twenty-four are Paige Hudson, Matt Warren, Janie Price, Paul Sagun, Jill Miller, Julie Caldwell, Chuck Patton, Eddie Smith, Kimberly Burns, Michael Colvin, Jeff Welch, Chari Beth Rose, Dan Knowles, Dwight Adkins, Laura Hodges, Jeff Stum, John Seiber, Marie Smith, Joe Leffert, Kyna Stinson, Daryl Pepper, Lee Ann Walke, Amos Gott and Ruth Hosse. It supplied five portraits on this run - Joe Leffert, Janie Price, Paul Sagun, John Seiber and Daryl Pepper - four of them replacing group crops of 1.8 to 6 KB. WHY THIS MATTERS BEYOND THIS BLOCK. The existing notes on Spirit Masters in _archive-gaps.json are all about the 2011-2018 BOOKLETS, which are closed, and about the scrapboards pairing by column, which is fragile. This is a different thing: a labelled composite. Nine scrapbooks exist at stu_org/321-329 and their record pages give the year each covers - 321 is 1989-90, 322 is 1994-95, 323 is 2001-02, 324 is 1985-86, 326 is 2011-12, 327 is 2004-05, 328 is 2007-08, 329 is 1996-97. Not all have a composite: the 1994-95 book has only an unlabelled collage of cut-outs round a newspaper advertisement, checked and closed. But 324 (1985-86), 329 (1996-97), 323 (2001-02) and 327 (2004-05) have never been opened by this project and each could hold twenty-odd labelled studio portraits for its year. THAT IS THE SINGLE BEST UNWORKED LEAD LEFT IN THIS ARCHIVE.
